question: What will be the Powerball Advertised Jackpot on December 31, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Jackpot is $687M for Oct 26 with no winner since Aug 12, 2026; $716M is projected for Oct 28. The next-drawing jackpot as of Dec 31 is the Jan 2, 2027 estimate, which reflects 28 drawings (Oct 28 to Dec 30). Per-draw win odds rise from ~5% to 15-20%+ as the jackpot grows, so surviving all 28 drawings is ~1%. The most likely path is a win in Nov to early Dec, a reset to $20M, then 8-25 rollovers, landing at ~$100-500M. A win early in the window gives a higher end value. The upper tail requires no winner at all. No human market found (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi none).

- Drawings are Mon/Wed/Sat. From Oct 28 to Dec 30 inclusive there are 28 drawings. Dec 31 is a Thursday, so on Dec 31 the advertised 'next drawing' jackpot is the Sat Jan 2, 2027 estimate (it reflects the Dec 30 result). If 'as of Dec 31 00:00 UTC' is read literally, it would be the Dec 30 drawing (one fewer roll).
- Mechanics: a win resets the jackpot to $20M. Post-reset growth example: $20M -> $687M over 31 rollovers (Aug-Oct 2026). Increments are ~$10-13M per draw early and ~$22-29M per draw at $650-700M.
- Per-draw win probability ~ 1-exp(-unique tickets/292.2M). Rough estimates (my hand model): ~5% at ~$700M, ~9% at ~$1B, ~15%+ at $1.4B+.

calls.reasoning: The jackpot is $716M for Oct 28 with no winner since Aug 12. 28 draws remain through Dec 30, and the resolving value is the Jan 2, 2027 advertised jackpot. The chance of a jackpot hit per draw climbs past 20% once the jackpot is above about $1.4B, so the current run survives all 28 draws with probability well under 1%. In the median case it is hit around draw 8 (mid-to-late November), leaving about 20 draws of regrowth from $20M, which is about $320M if no one hits again. A ~30% chance of a second hit in the fresh run pulls the lower half of the distribution down. No human market was found (none of the runs found Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmaker pricing).
calls.reconciliation: The facts are consistent across all three runs: $687M on 10/26, $716M next, 28 draws Oct 28-Dec 30, and the resolving draw is Jan 2, 2027. The 10/24 figure differs ($665M vs $674M), which does not matter. The no-winner result on 10/26 is only partly confirmed, but two runs report it and Texas Lottery lists $716M. The runs disagree only on judgment: how quickly hit odds rise (Run 3 is steepest, which means an earlier end and a later, higher regrowth... yet Run 3 has the lowest numbers) and how much weight a second hit gets. I rebuilt the hazard schedule myself. It puts the median hit at draw ~8 with about 20 regrowth draws, so the median lands near $260M, inside the runs' range of $205-285M because the evidence puts it there. There is a small ambiguity in the resolution criterion: Dec 31 00:00 UTC falls before the Dec 30 draw, so it could resolve one draw earlier. That shifts the value down by about one increment and is absorbed in the low side.
